text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx / gateway timeouts observed from inference-gateway-prod -> private-peering (count 5xx=120/min). Paging oncall for incidents channel. Impact: some Dedicated and Private customers seeing request latency spikes and 504s. See metrics: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/3060245678 :rotating_light:

sam-oncall: ack. I'm on it. Pulling up routes and recent configuration changes.

neha-net: I saw a spike in retransmits on the peering link ~03:02 UTC, and a small bump in MSS fragmentation errors on the transit appliance. Could be MTU-related.

jordan-ops: confirming 504s coming from the inference gateway loadbalancer -> peering egress. Canary traffic shows tokenizers time out after upstream reset. Logs: `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `TLS read timeout`.

sam-oncall: good leads. @neha-net can you run a quick tcpdump on the peering appliance for packets to 10.4.0.0/16? Also check if anybody toggled jumbo frames during last night maintenance.

neha-net: running tcpdump now, here's a short capture snippet (filtered):
```
16:03:15.123456 IP 10.4.12.34.443 > 10.2.1.78.52344: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, ack 1, win 60000, length 1460
16:03:15.123457 IP frag: 10.4.12.34 > 10.2.1.78: frag (DF), id 12345
16:03:15.223500 IP 10.4.12.34.443 > 10.2.1.78.52344: Flags [RST], seq 1, win 0
```
Noting a lot of DF set and retransmits. Seems like path MTU is smaller than sender MSS.

jordan-ops: interesting. We recently had a vendor push that set MTU=9000 on the transit appliance for throughput tests in a single AZ. That could break DF flows if the path doesn't support jumbo frames. Change history shows a commit at 02:40 UTC.

sam-oncall: ok hypothesis: peering path MTU mismatch after jumbo-frame toggle -> packets with DF causing fragmentation drop -> TCP stalls -> upstream closes -> 504s at gateway. Immediate mitigation: disable DF or revert MTU to 1500 on the transit appliance, or force MSS clamping on the gateway egress. Which is fastest?

neha-net: fastest is to revert the MTU change on the appliance (full revert), but that requires a quick config push and will momentarily disturb flows. MSS-clamp on the border router is lower-risk and can be applied without rolling the appliance. I can push MSS clamp in ~2-3 minutes.

sam-oncall: do it. @deploy-bot please hold any deploys hitting prod gateway for the next 10m.

deploy-bot: holds set for inference-gateway-prod for 10m.

neha-net: applying iptables tcp_mss_clamp on the peering egress: `iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu`. Pushing now.

neha-net: applied. Monitoring.

jordan-ops: metrics already showing drop in retransmits and 5xx count falling. 504s down from 120/min to ~15/min in 3 minutes. Latency tail dropping.

liaison-cs: communicating to affected customers: "We observed transient gateway timeouts impacting a subset of Private/Dedicated customers. Mitigation applied; service is recovering. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Customers asking if this was configuration change on vendor appliance; I need an ETA for permanent fix.

neha-net: permanent fix plan: revert MTU to 1500 on the transit appliance and coordinate with vendor to validate jumbo-frame path end-to-end if we want to re-enable. I can schedule revert at 03:20 UTC with a 2-minute config push and rollback window.

sam-oncall: go for the revert now. Notify if config push impacts other services.

neha-net: initiating revert: `ifconfig eth1 mtu 1500 && ip link set dev eth1 mtu 1500` then re-run path MTU tests.

neha-net: revert applied. Doing pmtud test (tracepath) to 10.4.12.34 -> showing stable MTU 1500.

jordan-ops: confirmed upstream connection stability. 5xx/504 counts now near baseline. No significant error spikes in the last 120s.

liaison-cs: relaying to customers: "We've reverted a recent MTU configuration change on a peering appliance; service has recovered and we do not expect further impact. Root cause investigation in progress."

sam-oncall: assigning owners: @neha-net will own permanence (schedule vendor validation and locking change), @jordan-ops will run full impact sweep (link-level packet loss and application timeouts across regions), @liaison-cs will prepare customer-facing timeline. I'll write initial incident summary.

neha-net: next steps: audit change management to see who approved the jumbo-frame test. Also add a guardrail to prevent non-owner pushes that change MTU on transit devices.

jordan-ops: will collect tcpdump + gateway logs for the last 2 hours and upload to secure incident bucket: s3://incidents/3060245678/trace.tar.gz

sam-oncall: good. any lingering elevated errors?

jordan-ops: small blips but within expected noise. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then transition to postmortem.

neha-net: putting a temporary policy in the config repo to block MTU>1500 on critical transit appliances and adding a CI check.

liaison-cs: thanks team. Customers asking about RCA timeframe — say EOD with full timeline?

sam-oncall: EOD is fine. We'll produce a postmortem draft and share to infra+product. Owner for postmortem: sam-oncall.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 5xx/504 rates returned to baseline. Severity: Sev2. Linking to runbook: https://wiki.redwood/infra/incidents/mtu-peering-506.

sam-oncall: closing thread when postmortem created. Great job everyone. :rocket:
